source_units.text:
# Socioeconomic Background and Self-Reported Sleep Quality in Older Adults during the COVID-19 Pandemic: An Analysis of the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA)

**Авторы:** Collinge Adam N., Bath Peter A.

**Журнал:** International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (2023)

**DOI:** 10.3390/ijerph20054534
source_units.reason: article_metadata_header
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: # Abstract
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The COVID-19 pandemic negatively impacted sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, research regarding older adults’ sleep quality during the pandemic has been limited.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This study examined the association between socioeconomic background (SEB) and older adults’ sleep quality during the COVID-19 pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Data on 7040 adults aged ≥50 were acquired from a COVID-19 sub-study of the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: SEB was operationalized using educational attainment, previous financial situation, and concern about the future financial situation.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Sociodemographic, mental health, physical health, and health behavior variables were included as covariates.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Chi-squared tests and binary logistic regression were used to examine associations between SEB and sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Lower educational attainment and greater financial hardship and concerns were associated with poor sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The relationship between educational attainment and sleep quality was explained by the financial variables, while the relationship between previous financial difficulties and sleep quality was explained by physical health and health behavior variables.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Greater financial concerns about the future, poor mental health, and poor physical health were independent risk factors for poor sleep quality in older adults during the pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Healthcare professionals and service providers should consider these issues when supporting older patients with sleep problems and in promoting health and wellness.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
## 1. Introduction

In March 2020, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the novel coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) outbreak to be a pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Since then, the virus has mutated into several variants that have spread around the world [1].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Common symptoms include fever, sustained coughing, and shortness of breath [2].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The virus can cause long-term fatigue (i.e., ‘long COVID’), injury to key organs, and death [3,4,5].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To date, more than six and a half million people have died as a result of COVID-19 [6].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, while undoubtedly severe, the consequences of the virus have spread far beyond its physical symptoms.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Notably, research has identified a general decline in sleep quality during the pandemic [7,8,9].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This is likely to be due to an increase in psychological challenges attributable to the pandemic [10,11,12,13], which may have disrupted sleep quality [9,14,15].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Broadly, disruptions to sleep quality are a primary concern for both scholars and health clinicians due to the overall importance of sleep.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: On the one hand, good-quality sleep has been shown to improve cognitive functioning, mood, and mental well-being, alongside allowing for somatic regeneration [16,17,18,19].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Conversely, long-term poor-quality sleep may lead to a variety of negative health outcomes, including dementia, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular complications, depression, and cancer [20,21,22,23,24,25,26].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: Given these detrimental outcomes, it has been important to identify those who are most at risk of experiencing poor sleep quality and to understand the factors associated with poor sleep so that interventions can be targeted to those in most need.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For example, it is now widely accepted that older adults are more likely to experience poor sleep quality than younger and middle-aged adults [27].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This is predominantly due to the natural compression of circadian rhythm waves in old age, which results in a decrease in peak melatonin production [27].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: As melatonin is the key moderator of the sleep–wake cycle [28], this natural biological change means that sleep fragmentation and arousal become more frequent, and sleep duration becomes reduced [29], thereby disrupting sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition to natural biological changes, it is quite possible that the negative relationship between age and sleep quality has been exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. According to Ring et al. [30], older adults typically have a heightened awareness of death, i.e., adults tend to feel closer to death in the later stages of life.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, this heightened awareness is likely to have been compounded by the fact that adults aged 65 and over have been disproportionately affected by the virus in terms of mortality [31,32]; this has been widely publicized throughout the media [33,34].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Consequently, older adults may be more likely to develop an overwhelming fear of COVID-19 [33,35,36,37,38], otherwise known as ‘coronaphobia’, which can present as anxiety, depression, and loneliness [39,40,41].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Such psychological adversity has been shown to negatively impact sleep quality [14,42,43].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Despite the well-documented links between aging and sleep quality, alongside the likelihood that this negative relationship has been compounded by the pandemic, COVID-related research has, so far, failed to thoroughly examine the relationship between aging and sleep quality within the context of the pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Instead, scholarship has generally focused on students, parents, and healthcare professionals (e.g., [44,45,46]).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Although such a focus is undeniably important, it has meant that older adults have been somewhat neglected in the literature.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Further, the extant literature focusing on age, sleep, and COVID-19 has tended to treat older adults homogeneously (e.g., [29,47]).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This is likely to lead to results that are too general; however, this could be corrected by accounting for further factors
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: Alongside age, researchers have identified socioeconomic background (SEB) to be a key contributor to sleep problems and health disparities.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In other words, lower SEB has been shown to be associated with sleep disorders, including insomnia, alongside overall poor sleep quality [48,49,50,51].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This is likely to be due to higher stress levels experienced by this demographic group compared with the rest of the population [52].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: These stressors predominantly revolve around increased economic burdens [53,54], heightened job insecurities [54], and childhood adversity [55,56], which is likely internalized and persists into adulthood [57,58].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Moreover, studies suggest that adults from lower SEBs are more likely to take part in behaviors that disrupt sleep quality, such as alcohol and tobacco consumption [59,60,61,62,63,64,65].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: Importantly, SEB, and any health complications associated with it, persists into old age [66].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This suggests that, when analyzing sleep quality in older adults, heterogeneity can be observed by accounting for SEB.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The aim of this study was, therefore, to examine the relationship between SEB and sleep quality in older adults in England, in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In doing so, this study is important in that it provides new insights into a previously underexplored area and offers new evidence to the growing discourse of sleep problems during the COVID-19 pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Materials and Methods

### 2.1.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Data

The data used in this study were acquired from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA) [67].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Since 2002, the ELSA has interviewed a large representative cohort of adults aged 50 or over living in England at biennial intervals regarding their health, social, and financial circumstances.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, ELSA also undertook a COVID-19 sub-study, which collected data on pandemic-related variables alongside the usual health and socioeconomic data.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The COVID sub-study had two waves.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Data collection for wave 1 took place between June and July 2020, and data collection for wave 2 took place between November and December 2020.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This study used the COVID-19 sub-study to assess sleep quality in older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Specifically, wave 1 data were used as the dataset and had a higher response rate (n = 7040; 75%) than wave 2 (n = 6794; 72%).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The data used in this study are freely available at https://www.elsa-project.ac.uk/ (accessed on 27 March 2022).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: 2.2. Sleep Quality
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The dependent variable used in this study was sleep quality, which was assessed using the ELSA variable ‘CvHesleep’.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For this interview question, participants were asked how well they had slept over the past month using a five-point Likert scale (1 = ‘excellent’, 2 = ‘very good’, 3 = ‘good’, 4 = ‘fair’, and 5 = ‘poor’).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This variable was recoded into a binary format for the analyses.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Original responses ranging from ‘excellent’ to ‘good’ were recoded as ‘excellent–good’ (=1), whilst ‘fair’ and ‘poor’ responses were recoded as ‘fair–poor’ (=2).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This split was based on the premise that good subjective sleep quality is determined by high satisfaction levels [68,69].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Conversely, ‘fair’ responses suggested that participants slept less than adequately, rather than satisfactorily.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Hence, ‘fair’ responses were considered to be more closely related to ‘poor’ sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Socioeconomic Background (SEB)

The primary independent variable to be used in this study was SEB.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, there was no single variable measuring SEB in the ELSA dataset.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Instead, SEB was operationalized using three proxy indicators: educational attainment (‘w9edqual’), participants’ self-reported financial situation in the three months before the coronavirus outbreak (‘CvPreFn’), and the extent to which participants were worried about their future financial situation (‘CvFinS_CvFinS1_1’).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Financial proxies were used on the premise that adults from lower SEBs tend to accumulate fewer savings over their lifetime, and therefore may be more prone to financial difficulties in old age [70].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To this end, greater exposure to financial difficulties and greater concern over future finances were considered to be indicators of low SEB.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Similarly, lower levels of education (i.e., <NVQ3/A-Levels) were considered indicative of lower SEB.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Neither of the financial proxies were recoded for the purposes of this study.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, the category ‘foreign/other’ (n = 573; 8.1%) was excluded from the education variable as it gave no insight into the level of qualification, and, therefore, could not be used to determine SEB reliably.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The educational attainment variable was coded as follows: 1 = ‘Degree or equivalent’ (reference category), 2 = ‘Higher education below degree’, 3 = ‘NVQ3/A-Level’, 4 = ‘NVQ2/O-Level’, 5 = ‘NVQ1/CSE’, and 6 = ‘No qualifications’.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The financial variable representing the participants’ self-reported financial situation in the three months before the coronavirus outbreak was coded as: 1 = ‘Living comfortably’ (reference category), 2 = ‘Doing all right’, 3 = ‘Just about getting by’, 4 = ‘Finding it quite difficult’, and 5 = ‘Finding it very difficult’.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The financial variable representing the extent to which participants were worried about their future financial situation was coded as: 1 = ‘Not at all worried’ (reference category), 2 = ‘Not very worried’, 3 = ‘Somewhat worried’, 4 = ‘Very worried’, 5 = ‘Extremely worried’.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Covariates

Alongside the primary dependent and independent variables, a selection of covariates were also included in the statistical analyses.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: These were categorized as either additional sociodemographic factors, mental health factors, or physical health and health behavior factors, and are described below.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Sociodemographic

Age, gender, ethnicity, and urbanicity were used as sociodemographic covariates.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The gender, ethnicity, and urbanicity variables were originally recorded as binary data, so further recoding was not required.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Age was recoded from continuous to ordinal data using the following groups: 50–59 years, 60–69 years, 70–79 years, 80–89 years, and 90+ years.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Notably, several participants were recorded as having an age of <50 years.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: As the required age to participate in ELSA is ≥50 years, these were deemed to be errors and these participants were excluded from the analyses
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Mental Health

Feeling depressed or lonely over the past week, and feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge over the past two weeks were used as mental health covariates.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The depression and the loneliness variables were used in their original binary form.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The anxiety variable was originally based on a four-point Likert scale (1 = ‘not at all’, 2 = ‘several days’, 3 = ‘more than half the days’, and 4 = ‘nearly every day’).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This variable was recoded into a binary format, where ‘not at all’ was recoded as ‘no’ (=2) and all other responses were recoded as ‘yes’ (=1).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Physical Health and Health Behaviors

Self-reported health over the past month, isolating due to increased risk from coronavirus, alcohol and tobacco consumption, and the presence of a longstanding illness, disability, or infirmity (LSIDI) that limits activities were used as physical health and health behavior covariates.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The latter variable was a composite, recoded from whether the participant had an LSIDI and whether the LSIDI limits activities.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Participants who reported no LSIDI were coded 0.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: If participants had a LSIDI that did not limit their activities, the response was coded as 1.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: If participants had a LSIDI that did limit their activities, the response was coded as 2.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The alcohol use variable was also recoded as 1 (‘yes’) if they drank alcohol or 2 (‘no’) if they did not drink or had never drunk alcohol.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Statistical Analysis

Descriptive statistics were first produced to characterize the study sample in terms of sociodemographic characteristics, mental health characteristics, and physical health and health behavior characteristics.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Chi-squared tests for independence were conducted to examine bivariate associations between the independent variables and sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Finally, binary logistic regression was used to determine whether the covariates had a moderating effect on the relationship between the SEB proxy variables and sleep quality in older adults.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In total, four regression models were produced.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Model 1 included and compared all three SEB proxy variables simultaneously with sleep quality, after which the covariates were added iteratively.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Model 2 also included the sociodemographic data, model 3 also included mental health data, and model 4 also included physical health and health behavior data.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: p values, odds ratios, and 95% confidence intervals were calculated to estimate the increased or decreased risks of variables and categories in relation to sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Variables that were non-significant in the bivariate analysis were excluded from the multivariate analysis.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Alpha was set to ≤0.05 throughout this study.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Data management and analysis were conducted using IBM SPSS v28 (IBM, Armonk, NY, USA).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement (PPIE)

The research for this study was presented to four members of a Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement (PPIE) panel as part of a post-graduate training scheme organized by Health Data Research (HDR) UK North.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Panel members were offered the opportunity to express potential research avenues for this study and which shape suggestions for future research.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Ethics

Ethics approvals for the original and subsequent waves of the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing were obtained from appropriate NHS Research Ethics Committees. The University of Sheffield Research Ethics Committee confirmed that this study involved only existing anonymized data and did not require further ethics approval (ref. 046081).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Results

### 3.1. Characteristics of the Sample

Table 1 shows the general characteristics of the study sample.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Among the 7040 individuals who took part in this wave of the study, just over half (n = 3726; 52.9%) reported having experienced good quality sleep over the past month.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The indicators of socioeconomic background (SEB) were relatively high in the study sample, with 42.6% (n = 2999) of all participants achieving A-Levels or higher, 61.2% (n = 4309) of all participants claiming to have been ‘living comfortably’ in the three months before the COVID-19 pandemic, and 77.7% (n = 5470) of all participants claiming to be ‘not very worried’ or ‘not at all worried’ about their future financial status.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The most frequently occurring age group was people aged 60–69 (n = 2348; 33.4%); 56.5% of the sample were women (n = 3980); the majority came from a non-ethnic minority background (n = 6726; 95.5%) and lived in an urban location (n = 5110; 72.6%).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Generally, the frequency of poor mental health was low, with 17.5% of participants experiencing depression (n = 1232), 17.2% reporting loneliness (n = 1209), and 36.5% experiencing anxiety (n = 2572).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Overall, 77.6% (n = 5466) of participants rated their health over the past month as ‘good’ or better, while 23.5% (n = 1656) of the sample were self-isolating due to an increased risk from COVID-19.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The majority of participants drank alcohol (n = 4596; 65.3%) and did not smoke (n = 6532; 92.8%), while 69.1% (n = 4871) of participants either had no longstanding illness, disability, or infirmity (LSIDI), or their LSIDI did not limit activities.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Three hundred and ninety-nine people (5.7%) had had a COVID-19 test; of these, 34 (0.5%) were waiting for results, while and 23 had tested positive (0.3%).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Bivariate Associations with Sleep Quality

Table 2 presents the results from the Chi-squared tests, which were used to examine associations between the independent variables and sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Regarding SEB, all three proxy variables were significantly associated with sleep quality in older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic (educational attainment: p = 0.005; previous financial situation: p < 0.001; and concern over future finances: p < 0.001).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition to these SEB proxies, the following variables were found to be significantly associated with sleep quality in older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic: age (p < 0.001); gender (p < 0.001); urbanicity (p = 0.004); all mental health covariates (all: p < 0.001); and all physical health and health behavior covariates (all: p < 0.001).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Multivariable Relationships between SEB and Sleep Quality

Table 3 presents the results from the binary logistic regression analysis, which was used to test associations between the socioeconomic background (SEB) proxy variables and sleep quality, in the unadjusted model (model 1, containing only the three SEB variables) and when adjusting for the sociodemographic (model 2), mental health (model 3), and physical health and health behavior (model 4) covariates.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Educational attainment (p = 0.321) was not significantly associated with sleep quality in model 1 and remained non-significant when adjusting for the other covariates (model 2: p = 0.551; model 3: p = 0.635; and model 4: p = 0.694).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Conversely, both financial SEB proxies showed a highly significant association in the unadjusted model (model 1) (both: p < 0.001).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: People who felt that they were doing all right (OR = 1.32; 95% CI = 1.16, 1.51), just about getting by (OR = 1.76; 95% CI = 1.36, 2.29), or finding it difficult financially (OR = 2.50; 95% CI=1.28, 4.88) three months before the coronavirus outbreak were significantly more likely to have poor sleep quality during the pandemic compared with people who were living comfortably.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Similarly, people who were not very worried (OR = 1.22; 95% CI = 1.07, 1.39), somewhat worried (OR = 2.14; 95% CI = 1.79, 2.54), very worried (OR = 4.11; 95% CI = 2.70, 6.24), or extremely worried (OR = 7.10; 95% CI = 3.19, 15.83) during the pandemic were significantly more likely to experience poor sleep quality compared with people who were not at all worried in the unadjusted model (model 1).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In model 2, when adjusting for age, gender, and urbanicity, both the financial SEB proxies retained a high level of significance (both: p < 0.001).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Similarly in model 3, when adjusting for anxiety, depression, and loneliness in addition to the sociodemographic variables, the person’s financial situation three months before the pandemic (p = 0.003) and being worried about the future financial situation (p < 0.001) were significantly associated with poor sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: When adjusting additionally for physical health and health behavior variables (model 4), being worried about the future financial situation remained significantly associated with poor sleep quality (p < 0.001), although the financial situation three months before the pandemic was no longer significant (p = 0.879).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In this final adjusted model, people who were somewhat worried (OR = 1.46; 95% CI = 1.16, 1.83), very worried (OR = 2.02; 95% CI = 1.15, 3.55), or extremely worried (OR = 8.09; 95% CI = 1.62, 40.30) during the pandemic were significantly more likely to experience poor sleep quality compared with people who were not at all worried.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In the final adjusted model, age group (p = 0.008), gender (p = 0.004), feeling depressed (p < 0.001), lonely (p < 0.001), and anxious (p < 0.001), and self-rated health (p < 0.001) were all independently associated with poor sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text:
Discussion

Using data from a large cohort study of adults aged ≥50, this study aimed to explore whether socioeconomic background (SEB) was associated with sleep quality in older adults during the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Further, it looked to examine the effects of additional covariates on the relationships.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The bivariate results indicated that educational attainment, the person’s financial situation in the three months before the coronavirus outbreak, and the person’s degree of concern over their future financial situation were all associated with sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: More specifically, lower educational attainment and perceived greater financial hardship and concerns were associated with poor sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
# Limitations

Several limitations became apparent whilst undertaking this research.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: First, much of the data were susceptible to recall bias [92] and under-evaluation [93,94], given that they were acquired using self-reported measures, e.g., the sleep quality and the perceived health variables.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Future research could seek to acquire data on sleep quality in a more objective manner in order to allow for improved accuracy.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For example, polysomnography could be used to measure sleep quality [95,96], although this requires greater resources and may reduce response rates.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The self-reported health measure we used is also subjective, and although self-reported health has long been established as an independent predictor of various health outcomes (e.g., mortality, health service utilization, and prescribed drug use) in older people [97,98], variables derived from a more detailed past medical history may provide a more nuanced understanding of the moderating effect of previously diagnosed physical and mental health on the relationships with sleep problems observed here.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Future research could seek to include data on such diagnoses from patient records.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Second, SEB was constructed using three proxy variables for the purposes of this study.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: While this provided insight into different components of SEB, it did not allow for holistic inferences regarding SEB to be made.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Future research should therefore look to use a single SEB composite variable, for example, through measures such as the indices of multiple deprivation (IMD) scale [99].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This may allow for more conclusive inferences to be drawn regarding the relationship between SEB and sleep quality in older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Third, the categories ‘BAME’ and ‘non-BAME’ were used in the ELSA ethnicity variable.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, these terms may be perceived as too generalized and may misrepresent the disparities faced by certain ethnic groups [100], such as Roma groups [101].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Accounting for the complexity of ethnicity by either using the terms ‘ethnic minority’ and ‘non-ethnic minority’ or by using a more comprehensive list of ethnicities may allow for more representative research to take place.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Fourth, the dataset used in this study did not account for the range of components that form sleep quality, including sleep duration, sleep fragmentation, and daytime sleepiness [102].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Adopting a narrower focus might yield further interesting results and may highlight greater sleep disparities as a result of SEB.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Finally, the two waves of data collection during the COVID-19 pandemic were relatively early on, and the data from COVID Wave 1 analyzed here were collected between June and July 2020, when relatively little was known about the virus and how it was transmitted. It is possible that the associations observed here may have been moderated or exacerbated as the pandemic progressed, or the findings may have been different at other times during the pandemic. For example, the UK came out of the initial lockdown period in June 2020; on the one hand, this might have reduced older people’s anxieties about COVID-19 (because the prevalence and risk of COVID-19 were reducing); on the other hand, the increased social activity and lack of rapid testing and vaccination may have increased people’s fears about being infected. These changes may have had a further impact on people’s sleep quality and on the relationship between SEB and sleep.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In the medium term, as the pandemic progressed, the understanding of the virus and its transmission increased and rapid tests and vaccines were developed, which probably helped reduce fears, although this may have been offset by the emergence of variants of the virus, e.g., the Beta and Omicron variants, which may have increased uncertainty and fears.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Further research should explore whether the relationship between SEB and sleep quality was moderated as the pandemic progressed, e.g., using the (smaller) ELSA COVID Wave 2 study or using other available datasets.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Similarly, a longitudinal analysis of individuals before, during, and following the COVID-19 pandemic would provide insights into both the effect of the pandemic on sleep quality and the extent to which the SEB–sleep quality relationship was moderated or exacerbated during this period.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Despite the limitations discussed above, the study involved a large representative sample of people aged 50 and over, and a number of conclusions can be drawn about this study that may be applicable to older people in other countries.

source_units.text:
Conclusions

This study is important in being the first to examine the association between socioeconomic background (SEB) and sleep quality among older people during the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic in England (June–July 2020).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: It has demonstrated that, in relation to sleep quality, SEB may need to be conceptualized in relation to component parts in order to understand the factors associated with poor sleep quality.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: In summary, this study found that lower educational attainment, greater exposure to financial difficulties, and greater concern over future finances were all associated with poor sleep quality in older adults during this phase of the COVID-19 pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, the relationship between educational attainment and sleep quality was moderated and explained by the person’s degree of concern over their future financial situation.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Meanwhile, the relationship between the person’s previous financial situation and sleep quality was moderated by mental health, physical health, and health behavior variables.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To this end, it cannot be concluded that low SEB as a whole was a significant risk factor for poor sleep quality in older adults.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Instead, greater concern over future finances as a specific component of low SEB, poor mental health, and poor physical health were found to be the biggest risk factors for poor sleep quality in older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Future research involving longitudinal analysis should investigate how financial concerns, sleep quality, and the relationship between financial concerns and sleep varied before, during, and after the pandemic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: From a practical perspective, the findings of this study highlight ways in which sleep quality can be better managed in older adults.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Principally, any financial concerns should be eased as much as possible.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: While this would probably be best achieved through state pension reforms, such political change does not offer the most practical approach for clinicians.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Instead, the establishment of free financial advice centers for older adults in areas of greater deprivation may help ease anxieties relating to future finances.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, such centers must adopt a person-centered approach, given that older adults tend to be reluctant to discuss personal problems with strangers [103].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Other possible options to ease financial strain during future waves of COVID-19, or during future pandemics, may be to provide temporary financial support to the people in greatest need, e.g., older people on low incomes.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In a similar vein, the provision of free and accessible mental health services for older adults should be made a priority in order to reduce cases of anxiety, depression, and loneliness.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Efforts must simultaneously be made to promote a mental health discourse in older adult communities, given that mental health is often a stigmatized or unrecognized concept for many older adults [104].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Finally, an active health literacy program could be developed in order to reduce preventable illnesses and behaviors that impede good-quality sleep, such as alcohol consumption, smoking, and obesity.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This study has developed important insights that could help healthcare professionals, policymakers, and health service providers to support older people generally, as well as during future waves of the COVID-19 pandemic, and in future pandemics more generally.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Healthcare professionals should consider the underlying financial or physical/mental health problems faced by individual patients who seek support for sleep problems: although poor sleep may be the problem being present, other associated factors may require consideration.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Policymakers and health service providers may wish to consider interventions to promote health and wellness among older people experiencing sleep problems.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
